acceptance: BH realised FDR <= pi0*0.05 + 2 SE in every cell
Bonferroni any-false-discovery probability <= 0.05 + 2 SE at pi1=0
Bonferroni power agrees with the exact formula within 3 SE in every pi1>0 cell
BH power minus Bonferroni power >= 0 in every cell with pi1>0

precision.metric: every headline number: FDR, power, any-false-discovery and power_gap_pp (as a fraction)
precision.reason: With R=4000 the worst 95% half-widths are about 0.015 for FDR, power and a probability near 0.64, about 0.007 near 0.05, and 0.01 or less for the paired gap; this separates BH FDR 0.04 from 0.05 and Bonferroni from BH power. The noisiest cell is m=20, pi1=0.05 with one real effect, where the gap itself is only a few points.

metrics.estimand: reference value pi0*0.05 with pi0 = 1 - round(pi1*m)/m, drawn for BH FDR (deterministic, no sampling error)
standard error of the mean over the 4000 repeats (and Wilson 95% interval for proportions) of each reported FDR, power, gap and any-false-discovery value

oracles.name: bh_superset_of_bonferroni
oracles.check: On one repeat at m=200, pi1=0.2 (fixed seed, chosen so the Bonferroni count is positive), sum three violations: Bonferroni rejections not in the BH set, BH rejections with p>alpha, and 1 if the Bonferroni count is zero.
oracles.reference: derivation: BH rejects every p<=alpha/m (rank 1 passes when p_(1)<=alpha/m) and only p<=alpha (p_(i)<=i*alpha/m<=alpha), so Bonferroni set ⊆ BH set ⊆ uncorrected set and the violation count = 0

oracles.name: bh_matches_scipy
oracles.check: Difference in the number of BH rejections between the script's step-up and scipy.stats.false_discovery_control (BH) thresholded at 0.05, on one repeat at m=2000, pi1=0.05.
oracles.reference: second implementation: scipy.stats.false_discovery_control, which shares no code with the script's BH

oracles.name: bonferroni_power_exact
oracles.check: Bonferroni power at m=200, pi1=0.2 over R=1000 repeats (fixed seed), computed as the mean of S/m1 from the simulated Bonferroni rejection mask, not from the closed formula, against the exact formula 1-Phi(z_{1-0.05/m}-2.5).
oracles.reference: derivation: a real test is rejected when z>=z_{1-alpha/m}=3.4808, so power is Phi(2.5-3.4808)=Phi(-0.981)=0.163

oracles.name: uncorrected_fwer_null
oracles.check: Chance of any rejection by the uncorrected rule at 0.05 when pi1=0, m=20, over R=4000 repeats (fixed seed).
oracles.reference: derivation: with all m=20 nulls independent and each rejected with probability 0.05, P(V>=1) = 1-(0.95)^20 = 0.6415 (E3); Monte Carlo se about 0.0076 at 4000 repeats

oracles.name: bh_fwer_all_null
oracles.check: Chance of any rejection by BH at 0.05 when pi1=0, m=200, over R=4000 repeats (fixed seed).
oracles.reference: derivation: when all hypotheses are null, FDR = P(R>=1) = pi0*alpha = 1*0.05 for independent uniform p-values, which BH attains exactly [18]; Monte Carlo se about 0.0035 at 4000 repeats

oracles.name: bh_fdr_upper_bound
oracles.check: Worst violation of the FDR bound, max(0, realised BH FDR - pi0*0.05), on m=200, pi1=0.2 over R=4000 repeats (fixed seed); tests the V/max(R,1) tally against the BH guarantee.
oracles.reference: derivation: for independent continuous p-values FDR_BH = pi0*alpha*(1-something) <= pi0*alpha = 0.8*0.05 = 0.04 [18]; the tolerance is about 3 Monte Carlo SE (SE about 0.003)

oracles.name: null_p_uniform
oracles.check: Mean of the simulated null p-values when pi1=0, m=200, over R=4000 repeats (800000 values, fixed seed); a wrong tail or a two-sided p-value would shift it.
oracles.reference: derivation: under E1 a null p-value is uniform on [0,1], so its mean = integral of p dp from 0 to 1 = 1/2; Monte Carlo se about 0.0003

criteria.name: BH superset violation
criteria.what: Number of Bonferroni rejections missing from BH, plus BH rejections with p>alpha, plus one if the Bonferroni count is zero, on the check case.

criteria.name: BH matches scipy
criteria.what: Difference in rejection counts from scipy's BH implementation.

simplifications.because: A fixed count round(pi1*m) makes pi0 exact, so the reference pi0*0.05 is exact.
simplifications.effect: Slightly lower variance of V and S than with binomial assignment; the mean FDR is unchanged to first order.
simplifications.probe: Rerun one cell with binomial-assigned real effects and compare the FDR.

simplifications.replaces: FDR as E[V/R] with R>0 only
simplifications.because: The standard FDR convention V/max(R,1) is used, as the BH guarantee is stated for it.
simplifications.effect: Includes R=0 repeats as zero; positive FDR would be larger at pi1=0.
simplifications.probe: Report the P(R=0) alongside, and note that FDR equals any-false-discovery at pi1=0.

simplifications.replaces: the realised false discovery rate as an exact expectation
simplifications.because: It is estimated as the Monte Carlo mean of V/max(R,1) over 4000 repeats per cell, since no closed form is used.
simplifications.effect: The estimate carries sampling noise of about 0.003 to 0.015 in each cell, so a value slightly above the reference can be noise.
simplifications.probe: Compare the cell mean with its standard error and rerun one cell with a different seed to see the spread.

simplifications.replaces: reporting only the chance of any false discovery when pi1=0
simplifications.because: The probability of any false discovery is also reported for pi1>0, where power is defined, so the families can be compared across the grid.
simplifications.effect: Adds columns only; at pi1=0 power is not computed and the any-false-discovery probability equals the FDR.
simplifications.probe: Check that at pi1=0 the any-false-discovery proportion equals the mean FDR in every method.

simplifications.replaces: uncertainty over repeats from a fully independent design
simplifications.because: Uncertainty is the standard error of the mean (normal 95% interval) or a Wilson interval over 4000 repeats from one seeded stream per cell, with no repeat-of-repeats.
simplifications.effect: Intervals are approximate for skewed or near-0 quantities such as BH FDR and Bonferroni power at m=2000, and for the one-real-effect cell.
simplifications.probe: Rerun one cell with a second base seed and see whether the estimates fall within the stated intervals.

simplifications.replaces: the exact expected BH FDR as the reference
simplifications.because: The reference pi0*0.05 is drawn as the guaranteed upper bound, and BH FDR is exactly that value only at pi1=0.
simplifications.effect: For pi1>0 realised BH FDR lies below the line by an amount that depends on the shift 2.5, so the line is not a prediction of the value.
simplifications.probe: Compare the realised BH FDR with pi0*0.05 across pi1 and check that the gap is positive for pi1>0 and about 0 at pi1=0.

protocol.seed_policy: One independent numpy Generator stream per (m, pi1) setting, derived with SeedSequence from base seed 20240601 and the setting index. The three methods are applied to the same draws within a repeat (paired).
protocol.failure_policy: No trial can fail in this simulation; any exception aborts the run and is reported. Repeats with R=0 are valid and counted with V/R = 0.
protocol.ci_method: Standard error of the mean over repeats (normal 95% interval) for FDR, power and paired gap; Wilson 95% binomial interval for any-false-discovery proportions.

model.summary: m independent unit-variance normal test statistics, a fixed number shifted by 2.5, one-sided p-values, thresholded by the uncorrected, Bonferroni or BH rule at 0.05.
model.holds_for: Independent z-tests; for independent continuous p-values BH gives FDR <= pi0*alpha, with equality only when the alternative p-values are 0 (e.g. pi1=0).

equations.derivation: One-sided upper-tail z-test: p-value is the null probability of a statistic at least as large as z, 1-Phi(z).
Bonferroni rejects when z>=c. For a real effect z~N(delta,1), so P(z>=c)=1-Phi(c-delta).

equations.formula: P(V>=1 | m0 nulls, Bonferroni or uncorrected) = 1-(1-t)^m0, t = alpha/m or alpha
equations.derivation: Independent nulls each rejected with probability t; none rejected with probability (1-t)^m0.

steps.name: BH step-up
steps.does: Sort p-values, find the largest i with p_(i) <= i*alpha/m, reject all with rank <= i.
relations: rejection set is contained in p<=alpha

steps.name: Error tallies
steps.does: From the mask and the truth labels compute V, S, R, V/max(R,1), S/m1.
